contexts.evidence: Sources, assertions, rights, identity reconciliation, and version-scoped review.
contexts.organization: Legal organizations, physical places, service organization, and resource capacity.
contexts.workforce: People, role authority, qualifications, privileges, availability, and assignment.
contexts.clinical: Patient identities/personas, encounters, observations, orders, care delivery, and disclosure.
contexts.workflow: Versioned pathways, decisions, prerequisites, events, queues, and resource allocation.
contexts.logistics: Inventory, medication and supplies, diagnostics specimens, transport, and equipment availability.
contexts.coverage_finance: Payers, plans, coverage, participation, authorization, rates, costs, claims, and settlement.
contexts.community: Geographies, populations, access needs, community services, discharge, and follow-up.
contexts.quality: Metric definitions, safety events, qualitative evidence, feedback, and measured results.
contexts.education: Learning objectives, scenario templates, immutable cases, disclosure, assessment, and evaluation.
contexts.simulation: Parameter applicability, stochastic dependence, experiment assumptions, and validation.

entities.definition: A versioned source artifact or endpoint snapshot with its retrieval and reuse context.
A contextual, attributed statement; its truth, author, review, and visibility are separate.
A decision by a qualified reviewer about an exact target version and use scope.
A versioned proposed or reviewed crosswalk between independently identified entities.
A legal or administrative organization, including health system, hospital operator, payer, or partner.
A licensed or otherwise identified care delivery establishment with a defined reporting scope.
A physical campus, building, wing, floor, room, or bed space; it is not a service team.
An organizational service/team with capabilities that may span several physical locations.
An individually tracked reusable resource, such as bed, ventilator, scanner, vehicle, or station.
Capacity at a defined instant/interval, with basis and counted scope preserved.
An identified real person or explicitly fictional persona; demographic identity does not imply behavior.
A person acting in a role for an organization/service during a stated period.
A documented skill, specialty, training, registration, or credential with verification status.
A scoped grant of authority for a role/person to perform specified activities at a facility.
Planned or actual availability of a role assignment; neither public identity nor affiliation implies a shift.
A real de-identified subject or synthetic persona whose facts are carried by attributed assertions.
A bounded care interaction in a setting; linked encounters form a journey.
A clinical meaning with optional versioned terminology mappings; code and concept are distinct.
A time-specific observation or measurement with method and interpretation context, not a diagnosis.
A request for a clinical or support action, distinct from its eventual performance.
A versioned procedure, test, consultation, medication administration, or support activity definition.
An actual or simulated execution of an activity, including incomplete and cancelled attempts.
A chart note, report, image, waveform, or document with authored and released times and access rights.
A scoped, time-bound consent/refusal decision with decision-maker and communication context.
A person-expressed or explicitly authored belief, goal, concern, preference, or barrier.
A versioned workflow graph with stages, permissible transitions, authority, and exceptions.
A contextual prerequisite, authority, routing, eligibility, or contingency rule with explicit effects.
A choice made by an identified actor, preserving available alternatives and rationale.
An immutable occurrence with occurrence and recording time, references, and causal predecessors.
A wait for a specified service/resource; entry, exit, and censoring are distinguished.
A reservation or active allocation of capacity, a resource, or role to an activity over time.
A bounded outage, shortage, surge, or absence affecting dependencies and available service.
A stock lot of medication, blood product, supply, or consumable with unit and expiry.
An auditable receipt, consumption, transfer, disposal, or adjustment of stock.
A collected or requested biological specimen with patient linkage and chain-of-custody events.
A versioned insurance product; benefits and network depend on dates and service context.
A subject-specific enrollment/eligibility assertion with period and verification state.
Date- and product-specific participation of a facility or professional in a network.
A request and decision for payer authorization with scope and expiration, not guaranteed payment.
A contextual amount with explicit economic meaning, currency, scope, and methodology.
A versioned submission for payment, with coded line items and adjudication state.
A payment, adjustment, denial, refund, or patient obligation associated with claim lines.
A review request for a coverage, authorization, or claim decision with time and outcome.
A versioned administrative or statistical area; place, tract, county, ZIP and ZCTA remain distinct.
An explicit inclusion/exclusion, geography, time, and denominator definition for a cohort.
A community or post-acute service with location, eligibility, accessibility, and referral process.
A patient-specific disposition plan, goals, readiness, blockers, and follow-up requirements.
A request for another service, placement, transport, or follow-up with acceptance status.
A versioned definition of a count, ratio, outcome, experience, safety, or operational metric.
A measured or modeled statistic with population, reporting period, suppression, and uncertainty.
An attributed theme, reported experience, exception, or practice from a described method and context.
A reported incident or near miss whose attribution and causal analysis have explicit review state.
An observable learner capability tied to expected context and evidence.
A versioned reusable teaching situation with permitted variation and completion rules.
An immutable authored patient scenario version, separate from real-world records and encounter state.
A versioned rule for revealing a case fact to an audience in an encounter context.
An immutable assessment rubric with applicability, observable criteria, scale and N/A rules.
A versioned judgment of learner behavior linked to specific encounter evidence and rubric.
A permitted transcript span, action record, answer, or observation used in assessment or review.
A reference test with inputs, expected behavior, prohibited behavior, and reviewer provenance.
An applicable numeric value or distribution with unit, dependence, uncertainty, and calibration basis.
A reproducible experiment binding exact input versions, assumptions, seeds, model, and outputs.
An evaluation with purpose, held-out evidence, acceptance criteria and limitations.
